en.html:
No.

Not so.
That was not what it had been.

Our vow that day.

We had acknowledged each other. Each other’s will.

Then I must no longer deny his will, even if acknowledging it meant acknowledging his guilt.

Muramasa’s slaughter was his crime.

And naturally mine.

Our crime.

Our crime, committed through our wills.

Caught in pity and my own guilt, I must not deny his guilt alone. He had not wished that.

Acknowledge it.

His will and responsibility, as I acknowledged my own.

We were two beings forming one warrior.

　私たちは互いを認め合った。

　だからもう、否定してはならない。
　彼の意思を。その承認が、彼の罪をも認めるものだ
としても。

　村正の殺戮は彼の罪だ。

　そして勿論、私の罪だ。

　<ruby>私たちの<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>罪だ。

　私たちの意志で為した、私たちの罪なのだ。

否定してはならない。
　そんなことを彼は望まなかった。

　彼の意思と責任を認めよう。
　己の意思と責任を認めるように。

　私たちは二つで一騎の武者なのだから。

en.html:
Ichijou"Oi."
Muramasa"May I correct that?"
Ichijou"Hah?"
Muramasa"We killed them. Milord and I, by both our wills."
Ichijou"..."
Ichijou"What is that... trying to escape responsibility?"
Muramasa"No. If you question Muramasa’s crimes and responsibility, I am prepared to answer."
Ichijou"Then we can do it here."
Muramasa"You are free to wish that."
Ichijou"What?"
Muramasa"I shall run, though."
Ichijou"You just said you would answer!"
Muramasa"This is my answer. I shall not resist you."
Muramasa"But... I cannot die now. So I shall run."
Ichijou"How convenient. You killed people without asking about THEIR circumstances..."
Ichijou"Does that not seem a little too convenient to you?"
Muramasa"...It does. So you may kill me."
Muramasa"Armor without a pilot against a complete warrior: the outcome is obvious. But... I shall struggle."
Muramasa"Almost no hope, still I shall struggle to escape and live. Yes... as those we killed struggled before dying."
Ichijou"..."
Ichijou"Why can you not die now?"
Muramasa"There is something I must do."
Ichijou"What?"
Muramasa"Restore Kageaki Minato’s will."
Ichijou"..."

Yes.

If I acknowledged his will, I could not permit his present condition.

Now his will truly had been stolen.

His mind’s shape had been altered by outside interference, not by a decision of his own.

I would restore it. His freedom of will.

I, who had vowed to be his armor, his other half.
